cues: Stanza three holds the poem's most famous line.
We are not wholly bad or good, who live our lives under Milk Wood.
The town in the play has a man who dreams of poisoning his wife, a woman who scrubs her house all day, a blind old sea captain in love with the drowned.
None is a saint, none a villain.
Thomas puts all of humanity in the middle.
The figure is litotes, understatement by denying the opposite: saying not wholly bad admits the badness first, and is warmer for it.
